extracted.intended_audience: journalists, reporters and copy editors (news writers) using Reuters style
extracted.subtask_description: A-to-C excerpt from the Reuters Handbook listing preferred spellings, word choices, capitalization, hyphenation and usage guidance for news copy. Intended as a reference of Reuters' editorial preferences for reporters and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Reuters preferred spelling, usage and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Reuters Handbook's preferred word forms, spellings, capitalization, hyphenation and usage in news copy. The Handbook lists entries alphabetically with explicit preferences and notes (e.g., preferred British/American variants, disallowed variants, guidance on hyphenation and plural forms, and guidance on particular terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Examples and specific preferences from this A–C excerpt include (not exhaustive):
- "allot, allotting, allotted" (preferred inflections shown)
- "ambience, not ambiance." (use 'ambience')
- "amok, not amock or amuck." (use 'amok')
- "analog, not analogue" (use 'analog')
- "anaemia, anaemic but anemia, anemic is American style." (note British vs American variants)
- "a.m." / "AM" (time styling shown)
- "altar, alter" (distinguish words with different meanings)
- "alternate, alternative" (preferred forms shown)
- "Aluminium" (preferred spelling; region-sensitive)
- "alumnus (man) alumna (woman) alumni (plural)" (use correct gender/plural forms)
- "American spelling" / "British spelling" entries (indicate style variant guidance)
- "ambassador" (entry for usage)
- "almost exactly" (preferred phrasing)
- "annex" (usage entry)
- "annual meeting" (preferred form)
- "antennae, antennas" (preferred form choices)
- "apparent / apparently" and related guidance (entries on word forms)
- "apostrophes" (entry flagging how to handle apostrophes)
- "appeal" (usage entry)
- "approximate/approximately" (guidance on use)
- "Arab names" (entry flagging naming conventions)
- "armada" / "army" (entries for correct word use)
- "around" (usage entry)
- "artefact, but American style is artifact" (note regional variants)
- "billion" (entry likely covers number usage)
- "biannual, biennial" (distinguish terms)
- "black box" (preferred compound form)
- "burglary" / "buildup" / "backwards (but American style is backward)" (various word-form preferences)
- "be with a present participle" (grammatical usage guidance)
- "beg the question" (usage note)
- "British spelling" / "British Isles" (entries noting regional usage)
- "brownout" / "bungee jump" / "blueprint" (preferred spellings/compounds)
- "capitalisation. American style is capitalization" (explicit note on American/British differences)
- "centre, but center in American style" (regional variant guidance)
- "call up, call-up" (hyphenation preference shown)
- "cancel, cancelled, cancellation" (inflectional forms guidance)
- "catalogue, catalogued... but in American style catalog, cataloged..." (variant guidance)
- "ceasefire, ceasefires" (pluralization guidance)
- "cellphone" (preferred compound form)
- "church names (e.g., Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints)" (style for organization names)
- "Chinese names" / "Arabic names" / "Burmese names" (entries on name styles)
- "cliches" (entry flagging spelling/usage)
- "chat room" / "chat show" (preferred two-word forms)
- "capsize" / "carcass" / "cargo and cargoes" (entries covering singular/plural and word forms)

Notes: The Handbook provides many single-line entries and brief usage notes rather than a formal multi-dimensional rubric; the practical rule for writers is to consult and apply the specific Handbook entry for each word or construction to ensure consistency with Reuters style. This excerpt is an alphabetical slice (A–C) and the full Handbook contains more entries and explanatory notes.
